articles.headline: Notice (Bishop Nazrey's preaching appointments)
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: Mr. Editor.--Please notice that I will preach at Bristol on the 30th, and at Trenton on the 31st of December, and remain over the next Sabbath to the Quarterly Meeting; and, on the 8th, I shall preach at Pennington, N. J., and at Louisville [place name as read].

articles.headline: Right and Wrong
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: Rev. W. R. Revels, who loves so much, only show your love by regarding the written law, and your love will continue. 1. Please read the 14th and 15th pages of the General Conference Minutes of 1860, on Canadian Affairs... (Nazrey's reply on the Canada / Indiana Conference question).

articles.author: Joshua Woodlin
articles.summary: Joshua Woodlin, pastor of the A. M. E. articles.headline: John S. Rock (biographical sketch)
articles.summary: A few weeks ago, we spoke of having paid the above named a visit. We now give the following particulars in regard to him. The subject of this sketch is a colored man, whose name is a household word among the colored people of this country. He was born in Salem, N. J., in 1825.
people: wife of Dr. John S. Rock; printed as 'Miss Catherine Bowers, an accomplished young lady of Philadelphia, and a member of one of the oldest and most respectable colored families of this country'

articles.headline: To the Memory of the Rev. Walter Proctor
articles.author: Joshua Woodlin

Many of the ministers of the Philadelphia District, itinerant and local, not less than forty in number, with some from the Baltimore District, formed in procession at Bethel Church, Sixth St., and proceeded to the residence of the deceased...
people: deceased (Rev.); died Tuesday Dec. 10, 1861; born Dec. 20, 1790, Maryland, near Port Tobacco; came to Philadelphia 1814; joined Bethel Church July 14, 1818 [year VERIFY: 1818 or 1814]

articles.headline: Notice (Frederick Douglass at National Hall; Mr. Anderson at Bethel)
articles.summary: We understand that the Hon. Frederick Douglass will lecture in this city, at the National Hall, on Tuesday night, the 15th inst. articles.headline: The Bethel Church Sabbath School
articles.summary: We, for the first time, had the pleasure of being present last Sabbath to hear the Bethel School catechized up in the state audience room; and, to the great credit of those who were candidates for the prizes, which Dr. Armstrong, a member of the Methodist Church, promised to give. There were seven who contended for the prize, and the number of verses committed by the highest scholar was over four hundred. Francis Seymour, the successful one, after the Doctor's remarks to him, replied as follows...

articles.summary: The birth-day of Rev. Richard Allen, the Founder of the A. M. E. Church, comes, this year, on Friday, which is the fourteenth day of February. Now, as his name ought to be held in remembrance, by the young as well as the old, we would suggest to all of our Sabbath School Superintendents and Teachers that they have their schools to give an exhibition for the benefit of the Christian Recorder...

articles.headline: How We Spent Last Sabbath
articles.summary: In the morning we were at Bethel Church, and heard a sermon from these words:--'Behold, I will come quickly, to judge every man according to his deeds.' Brother Eddy, who is a local deacon, not being well, spoke but a few moments, and we were requested to close after him. At 3 o'clock, P. articles.headline: A Sad Casualty (death of Samuel Woodlin)
articles.summary: The body of Mr. Samuel Woodlin, who resided in Thirty-ninth Street, and was employed as waiter on the steamer Isaac Newton, was found in the ice near Castleton, on the 26th ult. It is supposed that he was walking on the railroad, and the night being dark and stormy, he fell through an opening on said road, and thus met his terrible fate. He was a native of Philadelphia, where, we understand, he has relatives living. A wife and two small children are left to mourn his loss.
people: deceased; native of Philadelphia; resided Thirty-ninth Street (city not stated, probably New York); waiter on the steamer Isaac Newton; found dead in the ice near Castleton, 26th ult.

articles.headline: Lecture in Bethel Church
articles.summary: Mr. Anderson, who was announced to lecture in Bethel Church on the 16th instant, promptly fulfilled the appointment. At the hour fixed he came forward, and was introduced to the audience. He arose and spoke of the claims of the Recorder, giving a sketch of its origin, and of the importance of the press... Dr. Armstrong, being present, was called upon, and made some very pertinent remarks. A collection was then taken up, which resulted in the sum of $12.82...

articles.headline: An Example (bequest of Mrs. Ruth Hooper)
articles.summary: A good and Christian example, and the first of which we have any knowledge from a colored person in the direction from which it is bequeathed, has been set recently. Mrs. Ruth Hooper, who departed this life on the 10th instant, in the 84th year of her age, was a member of Bethel Church, in good standing. She had been acting as cook in the service of the late Mrs. E. H. Bray [VERIFY]. Through her industry and economy she had laid by some fifteen hundred dollars ($1,500)... She bequeathed for the benefit of the itinerant preachers of her Church the sum of six hundred dollars.
people: deceased Jan. 10, 1862, in her 84th year; member of Bethel Church; cook; left $600 to the itinerant preachers of the A. M. E. Church

articles.headline: A Card (Mrs. Hawkins' reduced prices)
articles.summary: We would just say that our friend, Mrs. Hawkins, is selling her stock of goods at very reduced prices. We would recommend, not only our citizens, but friends at a distance, Wilmington and other places, to patronize her. Now is the time to get bargains. Go to Mrs. Hawkins.

articles.headline: Prejudice (city passenger cars)
articles.summary: We are sorry to say it, but must speak the truth, the whole truth, that there is more prejudice in the city of Philadelphia against the people of color, than in any other Northern city. We have been in all the larger, and a great number of the smaller ones, but have never seen any to equal Philadelphia... But let a decent colored lady or gentleman undertake to get into any of the City Passenger Cars in Philadelphia, they must either stand in front or walk, if it is ten miles.

articles.headline: Our Paper (Brother Seymour's Sabbath School as example)
articles.summary: We do not wish to be considered as boasting, but we say that if we don't deserve the commendation and aid of our Church, and of our friends in general, why no one ever did. Many of our white friends in this city, and persons of other denominations, say that there are few men, white or colored, who could have shouldered and stood up under what we have done since the publication of the Christian Recorder commenced. Then, we say to our ministers and people, call your Sabbath Schools together, and do like Brother Seymour, in this city.

articles.headline: Revival in Philadelphia (Brick Wesley and Bethel)
articles.summary: Brick Wesley Church, the Rev. John A. Williams, minister in charge, is having a revival of religion in his church. The church was crowded to its utmost capacity the night we preached, and some appeared to be in earnest about their souls. This meeting has been going on for several weeks. Also, at Bethel Church, Rev. Joshua Woodlin, minister in charge, has commenced a protracted effort in his church, and has been going on for a week or more.
people: minister in charge, Brick Wesley Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notice (job printing at the Recorder office)
articles.summary: To all persons who may want anything done in the job-printing line, such as Cards, Bills, Circulars, &c., and in the best manner, with all possible neatness and despatch, we would say that we are fully prepared to receive and execute their orders on as cheap and reasonable terms as can be found elsewhere ... at No. 619 Pine Street, Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Letter from Bishop Nazrey (visitation: Freehold Circuit, Bristol, Trenton, Germantown)
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: I left my readers at Freehold Circuit; from whence I proceeded to Newtown, where brother Schureman, with a vehicle, awaited my arrival. We rode some six miles, and lodged with a friend that night. The next morning, being the Sabbath, we met the congregation in Allentown, N.J., and preached there in the morning to a fine audience; and from thence to Bordentown [VERIFY], a distance of eight miles ... I visited Bristol, Pa., on the 30th of December. Elder Robison was then entering on a protracted meeting ... My next point was Trenton, N.J. ... I visited Germantown on the 2d of February, at their Quarterly meeting. The people there have a fine little house, if they can only master their debt.

articles.headline: Notice -- funeral sermon of the late Rev. Walter Proctor at Bethel
articles.author: J. Woodlin
articles.summary: The funeral sermon of the late Rev. Walter Proctor will be preached in Bethel Church, by Brothers Rev. J. P. Campbell and James Fraby [VERIFY], on Sabbath, the 16th instant, at 3 o'clock, P.M. The family and friends are particularly invited to attend. J. Woodlin, Elder in Charge.
people: deceased (the late Rev.); funeral sermon at Bethel

articles.headline: Episcopal Visits (Frankford)
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: By the divine permission, I will be at Frankford, Pa., and will spend the Sabbath there, which will be the 23d inst., with Rev. R. Robinson. I will also remain with or on his circuit some two or three days, and should the pastor see fit to make any other appointment, we will attend to it up to the time above referred to.

articles.headline: Revivals -- Good News
articles.summary: We are receiving information from many of our brethren of the glorious work of the Holy Ghost among them. Bro. Wilkerson, of Leavenworth, Kansas ... Brother Trevan, of Richmond, Indiana ... Still the work goes bravely on. Rev. Joseph Smith, of the Burlington circuit, is also having a glorious outpouring of the Spirit of God ... Bro. Woodlin, of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, is also carrying on a protracted meeting, and some interest is being manifested. We also refer our readers to the case of Rev. Brother Gould, of Princeton, New Jersey.

articles.headline: Bethel Sabbath School Celebration (25th anniversary, Richard Allen's birthday)
articles.summary: The 25th anniversary of Bethel Sab. School will be celebrated for the birth-day of that great and good man, Rev. Richard Allen -- Tuesday, the 18th instant -- in Bethel Church. The doors to be thrown open at half-past 6, and the exercises commenced at half-past 7 o'clock. The price of admission is fixed at the low sum of ten cents -- the proceeds to be applied to the benefit of the Christian Recorder ... Remember, Bethel Church is in Sixth Street, between Pine and Lombard.

articles.summary: Brother Editor: -- Permit me, in behalf of Rev. J. G. Buleagh [VERIFY], to call the attention of the itinerant ministers of the Philadelphia Annual Conference District to the resolution passed by said Conference in the printed minutes, page 8, as follows, on motion: -- That J. G. Buleagh receive $5.00 per month from the Preachers' Fund, and that all ministers having charge of stations and circuits take up a collection for him in each of them, and forward the same to Rev. Henry Davis, Treasurer of the Preachers' Fund. We hope the brethren that have not attended to it will act accordingly, as Father Buleagh is much in need at present.
people: treasurer, Preachers' Fund, Philadelphia Annual Conference (Rev.)

articles.headline: Our Visit to Bristol on Last Sabbath -- Revivals, &c.
articles.summary: On last Saturday evening we left our place of residence to attend Father Robinson's Quarterly Meeting at Bristol, Penna., on Sabbath morning. Love-feast was celebrated, and it was a love-feast indeed, in the true sense of the term. Never before did we hear young converts talk more sensibly, or give a better evidence of the hopes they had of heaven. Brother Davis, a local preacher, gave us an exhortation.

articles.headline: Old Folks' Concert (reminder)
articles.summary: We would again remind our friends that Father Burris' Old Folks' Concert will come off on the 26th [VERIFY day] instant. It will be a rich treat. All lovers of good music should attend.

articles.headline: Died -- Miss E. H. Thomas (Lombard Street Central Church)
articles.summary: Died, in this city, on the 20th ultimo, Miss E. H. Thomas, formerly of Wilmington, Del. About seven years ago she became a member of the Hanover Street Presbyterian Church in that city. During the last four years of the period that she resided here, she worshipped with the congregation of the Lombard Street Central Church, and, by her death, this church, its choir and Sabbath School, have lost a true friend and a most efficient and useful laborer.
people: deceased (Miss), d. Jan. 20, 1862, Philadelphia; formerly of Wilmington, Del.; Lombard Street Central (Presbyterian) Church, choir and Sabbath School

articles.headline: Died -- Brother Titus of Rocky Hill, N.J. (Princeton charge)
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: Mr. Editor -- The painful duty again devolves upon us of recording the death of a beloved brother, Francis [VERIFY] Titus, who departed this life on Wednesday, the 29th of January, 1862, in the 46th year of his age. He was one of the founders of the A. M. E. Church, in Rocky Hill. He has been an exemplary Christian ... He has left a widow and four children to mourn his loss. (Signed Rev. T. Gould, Pastor of Princeton Charge; mentions a previous visit by Elder Campbell.)

articles.headline: Notice -- E. Weaver to preach at Union Church
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: At Union Church, on Sabbath, (to-morrow,) the 23d instant, Rev. E. Weaver, by Divine permission, will preach on the subject -- 'The six things that the Lord hates -- yea, the seventh one is an abomination unto Him.' Services to commence at 3 o'clock, P.M. Rev. Henry Davis, Elder in Charge.

articles.headline: Notice -- funeral sermon of Rev. Walter Proctor preached
articles.summary: The funeral sermon of the late Rev. Walter Proctor was preached by the Rev. J. P. Campbell, of Trenton, New Jersey, on the 16th inst., from Luke, 23d chapter and 50th verse -- 'He was a good man, and just.' The church was filled to its utmost capacity. We never saw Bethel Church fuller. The sermon was read by the speaker with much force and ability.
people: preacher of the funeral sermon (Rev.), of Trenton, N.J.

articles.headline: Lectures at the Institute of Colored Youth (Mrs. S. M. Douglass on Respiration)
articles.summary: On last Thursday evening (13th instant) Mrs. S. M. Douglass, the wife of Rev. William Douglass, delivered the fifth course of the winter lectures at the Institute of Colored Youth. Subject, 'Respiration.' At 8 o'clock she appeared before the audience assembled ... She spoke of the respiration in plants -- in birds -- and in animals, as well as in the human species.

articles.headline: Old Folks' Concert (Father Burris and troupe, Franklin Hall)
articles.summary: We would again remind our friends and the public generally that Father Burris and his troupe of musical artists will give a grand Concert on the 26th instant, in Franklin Hall, Sixth Street, below Arch. As this is the first concert of the kind, we feel quite certain that it will receive strong encouragement ... The main object of the entertainment is, the benefit of the Christian Recorder ... Half of the proceeds go to our paper.

articles.headline: China, Queensware, Lamp and Oil Store (editorial puff for Mrs. O'Donnell)
articles.summary: We call special attention to the advertisement of Mrs. O'Donnell, which will be found in another column of our paper. We would recommend the citizens of Philadelphia and others to call and examine her new assortment of lamps, China, &c. We are satisfied that they will not leave without purchasing. She is reasonable in all her prices. We love to see our colored people in business, showing that they are capable.

articles.headline: The Horns Taken Down (Bethel Sabbath School exhibition receipts)
articles.summary: Let everybody read this. At the Exhibition of Bethel Sabbath School the sum of $70.04 was taken in at the door. Of this amount $15 was presented to us for the benefit of the Christian Recorder by the Superintendent, Mr. Lewis Seymour, and the remainder went to the benefit of the school and the paying of expenses.

articles.headline: Anniversary of the Birth-day of Bishop Allen by the Bethel Sabbath School
articles.summary: On Tuesday evening, the 18th instant, the Bethel Sabbath School met to celebrate the birth-day of the sainted Allen. The church was crowded. The main audience room and the galleries were filled -- every pew being occupied; and many had to stand up in the aisles. The exercises commenced with singing by the school, assisted by the choir, prayer by Rev. Bishop Nazrey, &c. Rev. Stephen Smith was then introduced, who spoke of the Rev. Richard Allen with the zeal of a Paul.

articles.headline: Two-Cent Money (Bethel and Union church memberships)
articles.summary: We call the special attention of the brethren to page 210, New Discipline, in relation to two-cent money ... Suppose that Bethel Church, of Philadelphia, with over twelve hundred members, (we will say twelve hundred, though there is said to be some fifteen hundred,) should comply with the request ... The Union Church, placing the membership at two hundred, at twenty-five cents each, will give fifty dollars.

articles.headline: Bishop Nazrey, or the True State of the Question
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: In the 5?th number of this paper, we wrote an article upon the subject with which this is headed. We commenced that article by saying, within a few months past the peace and quietude of the A. M. E. Church has been not a little disturbed by the discussion of the question -- What relationship does Bishop Nazrey sustain to the A. M. E. Church in the United States? (Reply to Rev. A. W. Wayman writing as 'Presbuter'; dated Philadelphia, Feb. 1862.)

articles.headline: Old Folks' Concert
articles.summary: On Wednesday night, Franklin Hall was much crowded--more so than we ever saw it on any previous occasion. The attraction consisted of Father Burris' Old Folks' Concert. The curtain rose about five minutes before 8 o'clock, and we then beheld Father Burris and troupe seated, all being dressed in the ancient style...

articles.headline: Revivals
articles.summary: Elder Woodlin, of Bethel Church, closed his protracted meeting on Friday night, the 21st, with a general class meeting. He had quite a good meeting, and several joined the church. Rev. A. Stanford, of Little Wesley Church, is holding a protracted meeting in his church, and is assisted by Revs. John Morgan and William Fuller, who seem to be his main stand by.

articles.headline: Notice (St. Thomas' Church lecture and debate)
articles.summary: The young Quaker lady who was to lecture at St. Thomas' Church did not get there, as she received a call elsewhere. There was a strong debate between Mr. J. C. Weir and Mr. Alfred Green.

articles.headline: Episcopal Visits
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: I will be on the Westchester Circuit on the 29th of March. The Elder may make arrangements up to the 5th of April. I will then leave for Oxford on the Penningtonville Circuit, and remain to the 12th, on which day I will leave for Lancaster Circuit, where I will remain a week.

articles.headline: Letter from Bishop Nazrey (the Philadelphia Conference at Trenton)
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--I see that Bishop Quinn has given notice of his Annual Conferences, and also invited Bishop Payne and myself to be present at them. I would gladly meet the Ohio Conference if it was in my power so to do; but I fear that I cannot do it...

articles.headline: Meetings of Annual Conferences
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Annual Conference will meet in Trenton, N. J., on the 10th day of May, 1862, in the Mount Zion Church, at 9 o'clock. The New England Annual Conference will meet on the 31st day of May, at New Bedford...

articles.author: Presbyter

articles.author: Henry Davis; J. Woodlin
articles.summary: Philadelphia, Feb. 4th, 1862. A eulogy on the life, character and death of Sophia Rice, late consort of George Rice, was delivered in the A. M. E. Bethel Church, by Revs. Henry Davis and Joshua Woodlin, from Luke x. 41, 42. The theme of the discourse was, 'One thing is needful.'

articles.headline: Revivals (Little Wesley Church)
articles.summary: Rev. A. L. Stanford, of Little Wesley Church, is having a shower of heavenly blessings poured down upon his congregation. There have been several conversions, and the altar is crowded with anxious seekers, inquiring after Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

articles.headline: Union Church
articles.summary: Rev. Henry Davis, pastor of Union Church, has also commenced to hold a series of meetings since last Sabbath, and things are moving along very finely, we learn. At 3 [VERIFY: 3 or 8] o'clock, on Sabbath the 9th instant, Sacrament, and sermon by the Elder. The Lord permitting, we shall preach for Elder Davis on Sabbath evening, at half-past 7 o'clock.

articles.headline: Burlington Circuit
articles.summary: It will be seen that Rev. Joseph H. Smith has been having a great time on his circuit. A goodly number of precious souls have been brought to the enjoyment of God's love.
people: elder in charge, Burlington Circuit, N.J. (Rev.)

articles.headline: Appointments (Burlington Circuit quarterly meetings)
articles.author: J. H. Smith
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--You will please insert the following arrangements of my Quarterly Meeting of the Burlington Circuit: Burlington--4th Sab. March. Mount Holly--5th Sab. March. Evesham--1st Sab. April. Milford--2d Sab. April. Snow Hill--3d Sab. April. Jordantown--4th Sab. April.

articles.headline: Sacrament (Bethel Church)
articles.summary: Last Sabbath morning was the occasion of Sacrament in Bethel Church. The event was more solemn than usual. We cannot account for it unless it was because there was less singing while administering the holy rite to the numerous communicants.

articles.headline: Old Folks' Concert (proceeds)
articles.summary: Father Burris' Old Folks' Concert came off in commendable style on the evening specified. The sum realized by the evening's entertainment was seventy-eight dollars and fifty-seven cents ($78 57.) He presented us, for the benefit of the Christian Recorder, eighteen dollars ($18.) The remainder went towards defraying expenses for the use of the Hall and other incidental items.

articles.headline: The Cornish Society
articles.summary: This Society keeps a standing advertisement in the Recorder, and we must gratefully acknowledge the receipt of the sum of six dollars by the hands of their excellent Secretary, Mr. Seymour. Why will not all the Societies in Philadelphia give us their advertisements?

articles.headline: Hayti
articles.author: George Wells; Emeline Wells; Ben. Bacon
articles.summary: February 15, 1862. This is to certify that Hayti is a place not fit for any person to live in who has been accustomed to a residence in the North. I, George Wells, (and wife,) have been to Gonaives, Jacmel, Trinidad, ... St. Marks, and Port au Prince... One vessel called the Truxillo sailed from New York, with one hundred persons on board, and at the present time there is not one of them living.

articles.headline: Undertaking (Mrs. H. S. Duterte)
articles.summary: Mrs. H. S. Duterte's advertisement will be found in another column. We take great pleasure in referring our readers to this estimable lady as a person every way worthy of their support, and one well qualified for the faithful performance of the duties pertaining to her department as Undertaker... She keeps constantly on hand a large assortment of ready-made coffins. A very handsome hearse, with any number of carriages and drivers, always on hand.

Trenton, N. J., March 4th, 1862.

Returning from her duties, as the Secretary of a benevolent society, and being a woman of feeble health, sought shelter in the cars on Spruce St. near Tenth...
people: ejected from a Spruce Street horse car; secretary of a benevolent society; member of 'the Presbyterian Church'; tax payer

articles.headline: Trenton Circuit
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Lo! the winter is past, its rains are over and gone... During the last quarter, amid all the distress brought upon the land by the calamities of war, we have been greatly blessed. At Trenton, we have purchased a beautiful cemetery lot at a cost of $1700. The Rev. G. McMullen [VERIFY] Ladies' Sewing Circle held a fair during the holidays, by which we have realized a net profit of $70.

articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: On the first Sunday, March 2d, 1862, we preached again our discourse on the death of Rev. Walter Proctor, in the A. M. E. Mount Zion Church, in the city of Trenton, N. J., to a crowded congregation... We have formed here a society called the Daughters of Conference after those in the mother church at Philadelphia.

In accordance with previous arrangements, Thomas Lodge, No. 35, of Good Samaritans, Van Brakle Lodge, No. 4, of Good Samaritans, Smith Union Lodge, No. 13, of Daughters of Samaria, Olive Union Lodge, No. 27, of D. of S., Prudence Lodge, No. 30, of D. of S., and Perseverance Lodge, No. 42, of D. of S., was reinstated to fellowship with the Right Worthy National Grand Lodge... First Branch, on Tuesday Evening, March 4, A. D., 1862.

articles.summary: If no preventing providence should interpose, we shall leave for the Ohio Conference, which meets on the 15th of April, and we will preach in Harrisburg, Pa., on Thursday, the 10th of April, at half past 7 o'clock. Rev. R. P. Gibbs will please make the necessary arrangements. On Sabbath the 13th instant, we will be at Pittsburg...
people: editor, travelling to the Ohio Conference (as 'we')

articles.headline: Musical Association (Bethel Choir)
articles.summary: The Bethel Choir or Musical Association will give us some of their choice musical selections on the 27th instant, at the Philadelphia Institute, Lombard Street... The price of admission is only ten cents. Just drop in at our office and get a ticket.

events.name: Funeral of Rev. Walter Proctor, Bethel Church
events.location: Bethel Church, Sixth St. (above Lombard), Philadelphia; interment Lebanon Cemetery
events.description: Account by the pastor, Rev. Joshua Woodlin. Not less than forty ministers of the Philadelphia District, itinerant and local, with some from the Baltimore District, formed in procession at Bethel Church, Sixth St., and went to the residence of the deceased, accompanied by 'a noble band of sisters, known as the Daughters of Conference of Bethel Church'; a selected portion of the ministry bore the remains. In procession: the Bishop, Rev. Willis Nazrey, Rev. J. M. Brown, A. W. Wayman, and W. H. Waters. Street corners thronged with spectators, colored and white. The church was filled and officers closed the gates. Service opened by Rev. W. D. W. Schureman (1 Cor. 15); Rev. Stephen Smith gave out the hymn 'Rejoice for a brother deceased' and prayed; pastor Rev. Joshua Woodlin addressed the audience with Proctor's life: born Dec. 20th, 1790, in Maryland near Port Tobacco; came to Philadelphia in 1814 and embraced religion that year; joined Bethel July 14th, 1818 [VERIFY year] under Rev. Richard Allen; married 'in the same year, Oct. 31st'; present in the convention of 1816; exhorter two years, then licensed local preacher, then ordained deacon; 'performed more baptisms, marriages, and burials... than any minister now living in the A. M. E. connexion.' Woodlin and Brother Josiah Eddy [VERIFY] visited him after the first Sabbath sacrament of December and again Friday the 6th; on Saturday the 7th he called his family together (all present except his son John and 'daughter Barret'), asked his wife Mary to pray, prayed for his eldest son John and his daughter Elizabeth; on Monday whispered to his adopted daughter; died Tuesday morning, December 10th. Rev. A. W. Wayman then spoke ('Is it true, a great man has fallen in Israel?'). Funeral sermons announced: at Bethel, Philadelphia, by Revs. Jabez P. Campbell and James Frisby; in Baltimore by Rev. J. M. Brown; in Washington by Rev. A. W. Wayman. Remains conveyed to the Lebanon Cemetery and interred.

events.location: Bethel Church, Sixth Street between Pine and Lombard, Philadelphia
events.description: The 25th anniversary of the Bethel Sabbath School, celebrated for the birthday of Rev. Richard Allen, Tuesday Feb. 18, 1862; doors open 6:30, exercises 7:30 p.m.; admission ten cents; proceeds to the Christian Recorder; members of the school to perform. (Third notice; superintendent 'Brother Seymour' per earlier issues.)

events.name: United Beneficial Sisters of the Rev. J. Woodlin Society -- special meeting
events.location: Wealthy Dorsey's, Rodman St. below Tenth St., Philadelphia
events.description: Special meeting Thursday Feb. 20, 1862, 7 p.m., at Wealthy Dorsey's, Rodman St. below Tenth. By order of the President: Elizabeth Harris, President; Eliza Stokely, Secretary. (Changed/new officer names relative to the 1861 standing notice.)

events.name: Bristol quarterly meeting and love-feast (Father Robinson)
events.location: Bristol, Pa. (AME church)
events.description: The editor (E. Weaver) attended Father Robinson's Quarterly Meeting at Bristol on Sabbath Feb. 9, 1862: morning love-feast; exhortation by Brother Davis, local preacher; 2:30 p.m. sermon by the editor, after which Elder Robinson consecrated the Lord's Supper; evening sermon by the editor, every seat occupied by 8 o'clock, 'some thirty or forty (white and colored) standing'; nine joined the church. Robinson reported an eight-week protracted meeting on the Frankford circuit with about thirty converts; next Sabbath quarterly meeting at Bensalem. The editor took about forty copies of the Recorder and sold them all, plus new subscribers. Robinson described as one of the oldest itinerant ministers in the connection and 'among the founders of the Church'. (Surname-only references; per the brief, this Robinson/Robertson is Rev. Richard Robinson of Frankford; 'R. Robinson' printed in full in the Episcopal Visits notice.)
attendees: editor; preacher at the quarterly meeting

events.name: Bishop Nazrey at Frankford
events.location: Frankford, Pa.
events.description: W. Nazrey announces he will spend Sabbath Feb. 23, 1862 at Frankford with Rev. R. Robinson and remain two or three days on his circuit.

events.name: Father Burris' Old Folks' Concert
events.location: Philadelphia (Franklin Hall per the Feb. 1 notice)
events.description: Reminder that 'Father Burris' Old Folks' Concert' comes off on the 26th instant (date from Feb. 8 notice; originally announced for the 20th, in Franklin Hall, half the proceeds to E. Weaver for the Recorder).

events.name: Bethel Sabbath School celebration of the birthday of Bishop Richard Allen (report)
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Tuesday evening Feb. 18, 1862: Bethel Sabbath School celebration of Richard Allen's birthday; church, galleries and aisles crowded. Singing by the school assisted by the choir; prayer by Bishop Nazrey; address on Richard Allen by Rev. Stephen Smith; pieces and religious dialogues selected by the school's managers; two young men, Mr. Dingle and Mr. Wiggins, did themselves great credit -- Mr. Wiggins's theme was the Christian Recorder; Mr. Dingle is 'one of the pupils of Prof. Bassett, of the Institute for colored youth'; at half-past ten Mr. [Dr.?] Armstrong, a white friend of the colored race, spoke, saying the first missionary in the West was a colored man named Stewart. Receipts at the door $70.04, of which $15 was given to the Recorder by the Superintendent, Mr. Lewis Seymour. The editor claims the Bethel Sabbath School 'stands second to none in the city of Philadelphia'.

events.name: Funeral sermon of the late Rev. Walter Proctor (held)
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Funeral sermon preached by Rev. J. P. Campbell of Trenton, N.J., on Feb. 16, 1862, text Luke 23:50, 'He was a good man, and just'; 'We never saw Bethel Church fuller.' (The Feb. 8 notice also named a second preacher, not mentioned here.)

events.name: ICY winter lecture: Mrs. S. M. Douglass on 'Respiration'
events.location: Institute for Colored Youth, Philadelphia
events.description: Fifth of the winter lecture course at the Institute of Colored Youth, Thursday evening Feb. 13, 1862, 8 o'clock: Mrs. S. M. Douglass, wife of Rev. William Douglass, on 'Respiration' -- in plants, birds, animals and the human species; the editor commends it especially to young ladies and mothers.

events.name: E. Weaver preaches at Union Church
events.location: Union Church (AME), Philadelphia
events.description: Sabbath Feb. 23, 1862, 3 p.m.: Rev. E. Weaver to preach on 'The six things that the Lord hates -- yea, the seventh one is an abomination unto Him.' Notice signed Rev. Henry Davis, Elder in Charge.

events.name: Dorcas Society of A.M.E. Bethel Church -- warning against impostor
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: The Dorcas Society of A.M.E. Bethel Church warns the public that a female impostor is soliciting for the Society without authority. Officers: Sarah Carter, President; Elizabeth Oliver, Secretary. Dated Philadelphia, Feb. 19, 1862.

events.name: Father Burris' Old Folks' Concert, benefit of the Christian Recorder
events.location: Franklin Hall, Sixth Street below Arch, Philadelphia
events.description: Grand concert by Father Burris and his troupe of musical artists, Feb. 26, 1862, Franklin Hall; 'the first concert of the kind'; half the proceeds to the Christian Recorder.

events.name: Father Burris' [or Harris] Old Folks' Concert, Franklin Hall
events.location: Franklin Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: Editorial report: on Wednesday night [Feb. 26, 1862, computed] Franklin Hall was more crowded than ever before for 'Father Burris' Old Folks' Concert'. Curtain rose about five minutes before 8 o'clock; Father Burris and troupe seated, dressed in the ancient style, some with spectacles and canes, others with caps. 'It was well conducted, as the pupils were all perfect in the parts assigned them. Mr. Burris deserves much credit for his zeal and industry. The proceeds of the concert will be given in our next.' Surname printed Burris (clear in the Mar. 22 notice; one or two worn impressions here look like Harris); bare surname, so not linked. Probably the A. Burris, teacher of vocal music, whose card runs on p. 3 of this issue.

events.name: Protracted meetings at Bethel and Little Wesley churches
events.location: Bethel Church and Little Wesley Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Elder Woodlin of Bethel Church closed his protracted meeting on Friday night, Feb. 21, with a general class meeting; several joined the church. Rev. A. Stanford of Little Wesley Church was holding a protracted meeting, assisted by Revs. John Morgan and William Fuller. (Elder Woodlin = Rev. Joshua Woodlin, named in full in the Sophia Rice eulogy in this issue.)

events.name: Debate at St. Thomas' Church (lecture by a young Quaker lady cancelled)
events.location: St. Thomas' Church, Philadelphia
events.description: A young Quaker lady scheduled to lecture at St. Thomas' Church did not come, having received a call elsewhere; in her place there was 'a strong debate between Mr. J. C. Weir and Mr. Alfred Green.' (Weir is clearly printed; whether this is a misprint for J. C. White, i.e. Jacob C. White Jr., cannot be told from the item.)

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of 1862 -- called to meet at Trenton
events.location: Mount Zion Church, Trenton, N.J.
events.description: Bishop W. Nazrey's notice: the Philadelphia Annual Conference will meet in Trenton, N.J., on May 10, 1862, in the Mount Zion Church, at 9 o'clock; the New England Conference on May 31 at New Bedford. Members to attend strictly to the financial duties laid down in the Discipline. In a letter in the same column Nazrey invites Bishops Quinn and Payne to meet him at the Trenton opening, as the bishops had not met since the last General Conference. Bishop W. Paul Quinn's companion notice sets the Ohio (Zanesville, April), Indiana (Indianapolis, Aug.) and Missouri (Louisville, Aug.) Conferences. The notice repeats in later issues.

events.name: Funeral eulogy for Sophia Rice at Bethel Church
events.location: A. M. E. Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Eulogy dated Philadelphia, Feb. 4, 1862 (pp. 2-3), on Sophia Rice, 'late consort of George Rice', delivered in the A. M. E. Bethel Church by Revs. Henry Davis and Joshua Woodlin from Luke x. 41-42. Woodlin's biography: born May 23, 1793, in Baltimore; embraced religion at 14 and joined the Methodist Episcopal church in Baltimore; married early; mother of twelve children, six living, five present. In 1830 she came to Philadelphia and joined Bethel Church; a prominent member of the bands, she succeeded 'mother Dunbins' [VERIFY] as mother of the bands. Absent from the Band Love Feast on Sunday Jan. 26 through sickness; sewing as usual on Thursday the 30th; taken very sick about 4 o'clock Friday morning [Jan. 31, 1862] and died before 'brother Rice' could fetch her daughter Jane; daughter Sarah held her. Last words: 'Children, I am going home! Sweet Jesus!' Age printed as 'the 60th [or 69th] year of her age' [VERIFY]. Signed Revs. Henry Davis, J. Woodlin.

events.name: Union Church -- protracted meetings and Sacrament
events.location: Union Church (A. M. E.), Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. Henry Davis, pastor of Union Church, began a series of meetings on Sunday [March 2]. On Sunday March 9, at 3 o'clock [hour hard to read, 3 or 8; VERIFY], Sacrament and sermon by the Elder; the editor (Elisha Weaver) to preach for Elder Davis that Sunday evening at half-past seven.

events.name: Burlington Circuit (N.J.) quarterly meetings and protracted meetings
events.location: Burlington Circuit, N.J. (Burlington, Mount Holly, Evesham, Milford, Snow Hill, Jordantown)
events.description: J. H. Smith, Elder in Charge, gives the quarterly meetings: Burlington, 4th Sunday in March [Mar. 23]; Mount Holly, 5th Sunday in March [Mar. 30]; Evesham, 1st Sunday in April; Milford, 2d; Snow Hill, 3d; Jordantown, 4th. Protracted meetings concluded at Jordantown and at Snow Hill: 'Fourteen souls profess to be happily converted.' The editorial 'Burlington Circuit' in the same column calls him Rev. Joseph H. Smith.
attendees: elder in charge (Rev.); signs 'J. H. Smith'

events.name: Olive Cemetery Company quo warranto -- judgment for Stephen Smith and managers
events.location: Supreme Court of Pennsylvania (Chief Justice Lowry), Philadelphia
events.description: Quo warranto issued at the suggestion of Richard Wilson, John Dutton, Joshua P. B. Eddy, Francis Duterte and William Winters against Stephen Smith and others, managers of the Olive Cemetery Company, tried before Chief Justice Lowry; the Court entered judgment in favor of Mr. Smith and the managers elected with him. Text handed to the paper by 'Bro. Smith' from the Court. A contested election of managers of the Black-owned Olive Cemetery is implied. Followed up in CR 1862-03-22 p. 2 ('The Olive Cemetery Company in ...').

events.name: Revival services at Little Wesley, Union Church and Zion Mission
events.location: Little Wesley, Union and Zion Mission churches, Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. A. L. Stanford conducting a revival at Little Wesley; 'a number have found peace'. At Union Church (Rev. Henry Davis, pastor), last Sunday [March 9] 'father Richard Robertson' preached the sacrament discourse for Davis; at night the editor preached to a crowded house of white and colored, 'a hard matter for a stranger to tell whether the congregation were half or two-thirds white.' At Zion Mission (Rev. Stephen Smith, pastor in charge) the editor preached and sacrament was held in the after part of the day; sickness prevented his lecturing there on Monday night. Per the owner's ruling, the CR's Rev. Richard Robertson is Rev. Richard Robinson of Frankford (name recorded as printed).

events.name: Mrs. Palmer ejected from a Philadelphia street car (Spruce St. near Tenth)
events.location: Street railway car, Spruce Street near Tenth, Philadelphia
events.description: Letter 'To the Public' signed J. C. G. [VERIFY; could be J. C. C. or J. C. O.], introduced by the editor as 'An Outrage': on Monday evening March 3, 1862, about ten o'clock, during a severe storm, Mrs. Palmer, 'a highly respected and intelligent colored lady, residing in the upper part of this city', returning from her duties as Secretary of a benevolent society and in feeble health, sought shelter in the cars on Spruce St. near Tenth and was thrust out 'with the utmost rudeness'. She is 'a member of the Presbyterian Church, and a tax payer in this city'. 'This is by no means an isolated case. Will city papers please copy?' Not identified further; whether she is Mrs. E. A. Palmer of the N. Fifth St. dry goods store is not stated.

events.name: Dorcas Society of Bethel Church warns against a female impostor
events.location: A. M. E. Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: The Dorcas Society of A. M. E. Bethel Church cautions the public not to give to a female impostor collecting in its name; no one is authorized to collect for it. Signed Sarah Carter, President; Elizabeth Oliver, Secretary. (A Mrs. Sarah Carter is also president of the Daughters of Cornish Society per its standing ad; same person not stated.)

events.name: Trenton Circuit (N.J.) -- cemetery lot, fairs, donation visits and revival
events.location: Trenton Circuit, N.J. (Trenton, Pennington, Louisville [VERIFY])
events.description: Rev. J. P. Campbell's report, dated Trenton, N.J., March 7, 1862: the Trenton church bought a cemetery lot for $1700; the 'Rev. G. McMullen [VERIFY] Ladies' Sewing Circle' fair during the holidays netted $70; church debts cut to $250; the members gave the pastor a donation visit on February 5, his birthday; on January 23 the class at 'Louisville' [VERIFY; print unclear] held a festival for the minister's allowance ($27); on February 20 the church at Pennington held a festival ($23), and the Ladies of Pennington made a donation visit (a quilt, a young turkey, chickens). About forty conversions in three months. N.B. asks for 20 copies weekly. In a note below, J. P. C. reports that on Sunday March 2, 1862 he again preached his discourse on the death of Rev. Walter Proctor in the A. M. E. Mount Zion Church, Trenton, to a crowded congregation; 'We have formed here a society called the Daughters of Conference after those in the mother church at Philadelphia', who turned out in society order; two Doctors of Divinity of the M. E. Church, pastors in Trenton, attended.

events.name: Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria -- District Grand Lodge No. 2 organized, officers installed
events.location: not stated (city not given in the notice)
events.description: Six lodges (Thomas No. 35 and Van Brakle No. 4, Good Samaritans; Smith Union No. 13, Olive Union No. 27, Prudence No. 30 and Perseverance No. 42, Daughters of Samaria) were reinstated to fellowship with the Right Worthy National Grand Lodge of the I. O. of G. S. and D. of S., First Branch, on Tuesday evening March 4, 1862; under dispensation the R. W. National Grand Sire, Bro. George H. Hick [VERIFY], organized them into District Grand Lodge No. 2 and installed: James T. Robinson, R. W. P. Grand Chief; Mary E. Ashton [VERIFY], R. W. P. G. P. Daughter; Henry Brooks, R. W. G. Chief; Sarah Hosis [VERIFY], R. W. G. P. Daughter; Richard H. Gleaves, R. W. D. G. Chief; Mary Parker, R. W. D. G. P. Daughter; Nath. L. Durham, R. W. G. V. Chief; Mary Highgates, R. W. G. D. of the Fountain; James H. Smith, R. W. G. Prelate; Jane Pharis [VERIFY], R. W. G. D. of Lessons; Frederick C. Revels, R. W. G. Orator; Wm. H. Longfellow, R. W. G. R. Secretary; Sarah Jenkins, R. W. G. D. of Records; Jonathan Davis [VERIFY], R. W. G. F. Secretary; Cornelia Hilbert [VERIFY], R. W. G. F. Daughter; James Dolphin, R. W. G. Treasurer; Elizabeth Moeton [VERIFY], R. W. G. D. of Treasurer; Henry H. Gilbert, R. W. G. Conductor; Elizabeth Briant, R. W. G. D. Conductor; Wm. Cooper, R. W. G. I. Sentinel; Sarah Young, R. W. G. D. of the Key; George Murray, R. W. G. O. Sentinel; Susan Fanmott [VERIFY], R. W. G. D. of the Pass. Resolved that the list be published in the Christian Recorder and the Anglo-African. The city is not stated, so no names are linked; several names (Gleaves, Revels, Durham) suggest Philadelphia, but that is unconfirmed.

events.name: Bethel Choir (Musical Association) grand musical banquet, Philadelphia Institute
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Lombard Street above Seventh, Philadelphia
events.description: Announced on p. 2 ('Musical Association': the Bethel Choir or Musical Association to give choice selections on the 27th at the Philadelphia Institute, Lombard St.; admission ten cents, tickets at the Recorder office) and on p. 3 ('Great Attraction'): a Grand Musical Banquet by the 'Bethel S. Music Association' on Thursday evening, March 27, 1862, sacred music under the direction of Professor G. M. Galtat [VERIFY; surname unclear], with melodeon accompaniment, tables furnished with the delicacies of the season; tickets ten cents from the Committee of Arrangements -- Peter Brevon [VERIFY], Henry Gannon [VERIFY], Joseph C. Green [VERIFY], Jane Johnson, Elizabeth Oliver -- and at the A. M. E. Book Store, 619 Pine Street.

events.name: Father Burris' Old Folks' Concert repeated at Franklin Hall
events.location: Franklin Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: By special request of 'many delighted friends', Father Burris and his troupe to repeat their Old Folks' Concert at Franklin Hall on Monday evening, March 24, 1862 ('Don't fail a second time!'). Printed 'Burris' here (and 'Bunnie'/'Burris' in two places). Bare surname; probably A. Burris, teacher of vocal music. Not linked.

events.name: Bethel Church collection for the Port Royal contrabands
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Joshua Woodlin, Elder in Charge, announces a collection in Bethel Church on Sunday March 23, 1862 in aid of the Port Royal contrabands: preaching at 10 A.M. by the pastor, at 3 P.M. by Rev. A. L. Stanford of Little Wesley Church, at half-past 7 by Rev. James Gloucester of New York. 'Let the members of the church and congregation come prepared to contribute to this laudable and humane object, and receive the blessings of the destitute bondman.' (Gloucester is a New Yorker; linked here only as a named preacher at a Philadelphia event, as printed.)

events.name: Olive Cemetery Company quo warranto -- rival notice claims verdict for the plaintiffs
events.location: Philadelphia (court not named)
events.description: Two weeks after the CR printed (Mar. 8) Stephen Smith's version, that the court gave judgment for Smith and the managers elected with him, this notice signed 'L. Hubbert [VERIFY], No. 518 [VERIFY] Sixth Street' states that in the same quo warranto, at the suggestion of Richard Wilson, John Dutton, Joshua P. B. Eddy, Francis Duterte and William Winters against Stephen Smith and others, managers of the Olive Cemetery Company, 'verdict was entered for the plaintiffs, Richard Wilson, and others.' The two printed accounts contradict each other (perhaps a jury verdict versus a later judgment); the court record should be checked.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association -- Port Royal freedmen relief: subscription and Executive Committee resolutions
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Philadelphia (resolutions); receiving points 711 Lombard, 107 N. Fifth, 619 Pine
events.description: The Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania opened a subscription for the freedmen at Port Royal, to be acknowledged in the Recorder; subscriptions to Jacob C. White at the office of the Lebanon Cemetery, 711 Lombard St., William Still, 107 N. Fifth St., or Rev. E. Weaver, 619 Pine St. PAID: Statistical Society $50; Clayton Miller $2; William Still $5; Robert Adger $2; Henry Minturn $2; Catherine Johnson $2; Vasti Locke $2; Wm. Warricks $2; Harriet Shorter $1; Sarah S. Hawkins $1; Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs $1; James P. Clay $1. 'Port Royal Contrabands': at a meeting held Wednesday evening at the Philadelphia Institute, the Executive Committee of the Statistical Association passed resolutions, read at the close of a concert by the Hutchinson Family 'last evening' given in aid of the escaped slaves at Port Royal: the contrabands' claims call loudly for aid; though the Government has not fully defined their status, the Association should aid them and commend them to the colored churches and societies of the city and State to co-operate with the Freedmen's Association or similar enterprises furnishing food, clothing and teachers; in view of the Act of Congress and the generals' proclamations, the slaves 'cannot (in our judgment) be considered other than FREEMEN.' Signed J. C. Wears, President; Wm. Still, Corresponding Secretary; S. M. Smith, Recording Secretary.
attendees: president, Social, Civil and Statistical Association (printed 'J. C. Wears') (printed 'J. C. Wears')
receiver of subscriptions, Lebanon Cemetery office

events.name: A. M. E. General Committee called to meet at Bethel Church
events.location: Bethel Church (minister's study), Philadelphia
events.description: E. Weaver, Book Steward and Editor, notifies the General Committee to meet on May 8, 1862, at 9 A.M., in the minister's study of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, two days before the Philadelphia Annual Conference opens at Trenton.

events.name: Sunday preaching appointments at Bethel Church and Zion Mission
events.location: Bethel Church and Zion Mission Church, Philadelphia
events.description: J. Woodlin, Elder in charge of Bethel, announces for Sunday March 30, 1862: Rev. S. T. Jones of Harrisburg, Pa., at 10 1/2 A.M.; Rev. E. Weaver, General Book Steward, at 3 P.M. (Deut. iv. 9: 'Only take heed to thyself, and keep thy soul diligently...'); Rev. J. C. Gibbs 'of the Presbyterian' [church] at 7 1/2 P.M. Rev. J. Woodlin of Bethel to preach at Zion Mission Church at 10 1/2 A.M. the same day. (S. T. Jones of Harrisburg mentioned only.) Per the brief, any 1860s Gibbs is Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs (the son).
attendees: elder in charge, Bethel; preacher at Zion Mission

events.name: United Beneficial Sisters of the Rev. J. Woodlin Society -- first anniversary
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Lombard Street above Seventh, Philadelphia
events.description: First anniversary of the United Beneficial Sisters of the Rev. J. Woodlin Society, Thursday evening April 10, 1862, 8 o'clock, at the Philadelphia Institute. Members to meet first on the first Thursday evening in April [Apr. 3] at Sister Dorsey's [VERIFY] in Rodman St. Signed E. Harris [VERIFY], President; E. Stokeley [VERIFY], Secretary. (The society's standing notice was captured in the 1861 runs; this anniversary is new.)

events.name: Editor and Bishop Nazrey visit Burlington, N.J. (love feast, sacrament, preaching)
events.location: A. M. E. church, Burlington, N.J.
events.description: On Sunday [March 23, 1862] the editor and Bishop Nazrey took the boat to Burlington, arriving about 10 A.M. during a love feast; Rev. Joseph [H.] Smith, elder in charge, seated them in the pulpit; old gray-headed fathers and mothers spoke. Smith and the Bishop had the editor preach morning and night; Bishop Nazrey administered the Lord's Supper and preached at 3 P.M. on 'There is a river, the streams whereof make glad the city of God' (he said he felt more like old times in Phila. than he had for a long time). The congregation prays that Smith be returned, and wants Burlington made a station, as should Trenton, Bordentown, Gouldtown and Salem. Rev. W. D. W. Schureman's wife is lying very low, not expected to live many days; the editor called on her three times in Burlington.

David Cole [VERIFY] at a Sabbath School Convention in Camden, N. Masonic notice (Burlington, N.J., counts as Philadelphia Conference territory): the image is very faint; only names read with confidence are linked. Joshua Woodlin is pastor of Bethel, Philadelphia.

CR_1862-01-11 p1: masthead now 'Rev. Elisha Weaver, Editor' (Weaver resumed editorship); corresponding editors list; selections (Mohammedan mosques, Pope, Sabbath-school library, 'Trust in the Lord', 'Eternity of the Wicked', Breckinridge on the war, self-government). Nothing in scope.

CR_1862-01-11 p2: also 'Where are Bishops Payne and Quinn?' (editorial); 'Class Meetings' essay; 'Letter from Bishop Nazrey' to the members of the General Conference of 1860 on the Canada (B. M. E.) separation; 'Letter from Brother R. H. Cain' (Brooklyn, Dec. 29th 1861; Brooklyn Sabbath-school Christmas exhibition -- names in it are Brooklyn/New York, not entered); 'Our Say' (signed Justice, from the Anglo-African); a reply to 'Mr. Observer' defending Bishop Nazrey's Canada course. 'Linda' notice: Mrs. Jacobs (Harriet Jacobs, Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl) selling her book in Philadelphia at No. 107 North Fifth St. (William Still's address) -- not linked as she is of New York.

Grand Lodge (p2): this is the Philadelphia Black Masonic Grand Lodge (hall on South Eleventh below Pine). 'James Needham' is printed without middle initial; per the owner's rule plain 'James Needham' is the father, 'James F. Needham' the son -- in 1861 a living R. W. G. M. may be either; recorded as printed, identification left open. 'S. Morgan Smith' = Rev. Stephen Smith (recorded as printed). Aaron P. Faucett printed 'Faucett' in the list and 'Faucett' in the attest.

Douglass/Anderson notice dates: printed 'Tuesday night, the 15th inst.' and 'Thursday night, the 17th inst.'; in January 1862 the 15th was a Wednesday and the 17th a Friday. Event date set to the printed Thursday's computed date is unreliable; see flags.

CR_1862-01-11 p3: Mrs. E. A. Palmer's changed ad ('Dry Goods and Trimmings Store', 105 N. Fifth) entered once here. William Still now runs a 'COAL! COAL!! COAL!!!' price ad (Lehigh and Schuylkill coal; orders at the Stove Store, 107 North Fifth St.) -- Still's coal/stove business already captured, not re-entered. 'Good News' tailoring-system ad gives Mrs. Mary [?] Weaver, wife of the editor, as agent at 619 Pine. Other recurring ads not re-entered; Perry & Fitzgerald's bread, Van Riper & Camp, T. S. Knight, Keely's gallery etc. out of scope. News columns: war items (white chaplains Rev. Charles Woodward, Rev. J. C. Cromack -- out of scope).
CR_1862-01-11 p4: all white commercial ads plus reprinted reading; the 'N. ? Burnett, Watch Maker and Jeweller' ad is illegible on this reel.
CR_1862-01-18 p1: masthead and selections only ('This Year Thou Shalt Die', 'The Convict's Return', 'The Number Seven', 'Advice on Pulpit Speaking', etc.). Nothing in scope.

CR_1862-01-18 p2: Notices of Annual Conferences repeated (entered Jan. 11). Also 'Revivals' (Rev. F. Myers, Bloomington circuit, Ill.; Rev. Wm. J. Davis, Jacksonville, Ill.), 'North-Western Christian Advocate' and missionary items (white/foreign), 'Subscription List' editorial, letters from Rev. W. W. Grimes (New Bedford) and Rev. W. J. Davis (Jacksonville, Ill.), 'An Unkind Spirit', end of A. Fields' letter, 'The Letter from Rev. J. P. Campbell' (editorial note), and the full text of Douglass's 'The Great Speech' (cols 5-7). Non-Philadelphia names not entered.
